reuse.why: All month-wide actions, including the new setLastMonthSpending, take their categories from the existing getBulkBudgetCategories and the new action reuses averageToBudget, getSheetValue, batchMessages and the mutator/undoable registration.

duplication.why: Exclusion rules are written once in the shared selector; only the new action's batch loop over categories mirrors set3MonthAvg's loop, which is the tree's normal shape.

placement.why: Selection rules live in getBulkBudgetCategories in budget/actions.ts, the new action next to the other bulk actions and its handler registered in budget/app.ts.

scope.why: Only the bulk-selection rule, the per-action flag, the new action and its tests are touched.

maintainability.why: One place decides which categories bulk actions write, so each new rule (#fixed, templates, hidden flag) is a single edit; the '#fixed' regex is inline rather than named, and the includeHidden early return quietly skips the skipMissingGroup check.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every month-wide action calls getBulkBudgetCategories; none filters categories on its own.

disguised_duplication.where: The only repeated shape is the category loop in setLastMonthSpending, written openly like set3MonthAvg's.

abstraction_drift.where: getBulkBudgetCategories keeps its existing includeHidden/skipMissingGroup parameters; the #fixed and saved-template exclusions are general rule clauses for all callers, and the per-action includeHiddenCategories flag is just forwarded to the existing parameter.
